create.title: Create FTP Account
create.subtitle: Give a client FTP access to one website's directory.
create.detailsHelp: The account is locked to the chosen directory. Passwords are never stored in dPanel, so copy it before you save.
create.usernameHelp: Starts with {prefix}; lowercase letters, numbers and underscores.

index.deleteConfirm: Delete FTP account {user}? Client access will stop immediately.
index.title: FTP Accounts
index.subtitle: Every FTP account across your websites.
index.noMatch: No FTP accounts match this filter.

connect.subtitle: Check the FTP server and set up a client.
connect.testHelp: Connects to {host}:{port} the way a client would. To test one account's login, open it from Accounts.
connect.testHelpTls: Connects to {host}:{port} the way a client would and checks that TLS is offered. To test one account's login, open it from Accounts.
connect.clientHelp: Use these in any FTP client. Security: {security}.
connect.guideHelp: What this server needs so FTP clients can connect. Values are read from this server.
connect.downloadHelp: Free clients that support FTP over TLS. Each account's Manage page also has a ready-made FileZilla config.

guide.how: Port {port} only carries commands: login, change folder, delete. Every folder listing and file transfer opens a second connection to one of the passive ports ({range}). If those ports cannot be reached, login works but listing and uploads fail.
guide.routerTitle: Forward the ports on your router
guide.router: This server sits behind a router ({ip}), so the internet reaches the router, not the server. Add these port forwarding rules on the router. The menu is usually called Port Forwarding, Virtual Server or NAT (TP-Link: Advanced → NAT Forwarding → Virtual Servers).
guide.fixedIp: Give this server a fixed IP ({ip}) in the router's DHCP settings, or the rules stop working when it changes.
guide.shrink: If the router cannot forward a range this large, shrink it: {cmd}, then forward that range.
guide.ipChange: If your internet provider changes the public IP, run {cmd} so FTP announces the new one.
guide.fwTitle: Open the ports in the firewall
guide.fw: Allow TCP {port} and TCP {range} inbound. {cmd} opens them in ufw on this server. If your provider has its own firewall (security group, cloud firewall), open the same ports there too.
guide.hairpin: This server cannot reach its own public IP ({ip}), which many routers do not allow. That does not mean clients are blocked. Connect from a computer on another network (for example a phone hotspot) with FileZilla to check.
guide.pub: FTP does not know this server's public IP, so it tells clients an address they cannot reach. Run {cmd}.

manage.copyNow: Copy it now; it is not stored.
manage.filezillaHelp: File → Import, choose the downloaded file. It asks for the password when you connect.
manage.vscodeHelp: install the {ext}, save the file as {file} in your project folder and put the password in its {field} field. Then run "SFTP: Download Project" from the command palette. Keep {file} out of git.
manage.testHelp: Logs in as this account from the server and lists its directory. The password is only used for this test.
manage.changePwHelp: Takes effect immediately. Connected clients must log in again.
manage.deleteHelp: Removes FTP access. Files in {dir} are not touched.

clients.vscodePlatforms: VS Code extension, edit files in place
